title: The People Challenge Alma
summary: The people question Alma’s authority and say they will not believe his warnings about the earth or their city. The narration says they do not understand and are hard-hearted.

explicit_facts.text: The people question whether they should believe one man who preaches that the earth will pass away.
They do not understand their own words and do not know that the earth will pass away.
They say they will not believe Alma if he prophesies that the city will be destroyed in one day.
They do not know that God can do marvelous works, and are described as hard-hearted and stiffnecked.

title: Alma Rebukes Their Forgetfulness
summary: Alma asks whether they have forgotten the commandments and recounts Lehi’s deliverance from Jerusalem, the journey through the wilderness, and deliverance from enemies. He says God’s power and mercy preserved their fathers.

explicit_facts.text: Alma rebukes the people for forgetting their fathers’ tradition and God’s commandments.
Alma recalls that Lehi was brought out of Jerusalem by God and led through the wilderness.
Alma recalls deliverances of their fathers from enemies, including their own brethren.
Alma says God’s power, mercy, and long-suffering prevented their people from being cut off earlier.

title: Call to Repent

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says those addressed are commanded to repent and cannot inherit the kingdom of God unless they repent.
The speaker warns of utter destruction and visitation in anger if those addressed do not repent.
The speaker recalls words spoken to Lehi stating that keeping the commandments brings prosperity in the land.
The speaker separately introduces with 'And again it is said that:' a saying that those who do not keep the commandments shall be cut off from the presence of the Lord.

title: Alma Compares Their Accountability
summary: Alma says the Lamanites have been cut off from the Lord’s presence, yet will receive mercy and future promises; he warns that the people of Ammonihah face greater consequences if they remain in sin.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the Lamanites have been cut off from the Lord’s presence because of transgression.
Alma says judgment and this life will be more tolerable for the Lamanites than for the people if the latter do not repent.
Alma says the Lord will be merciful to the Lamanites and prolong their existence in the land because of their fathers’ traditions.
Alma says many Lamanites will eventually believe and be saved, and the Lord will be merciful to those who call on his name.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks to the people in Ammonihah.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lamanites are mentioned in speech but are not described as present.

title: Warning of Destruction
summary: Alma warns that persistent wickedness will bring destruction and the Lamanites upon the people. He emphasizes their greater light, knowledge, gifts, deliverances, and blessings, and says rebellion would make their destruction less tolerable.

explicit_facts.text: Alma warns that if the people persist in wickedness, the Lamanites will be sent upon them and they will face destruction if they do not repent.
Alma says God would rather suffer the Lamanites to destroy the Nephite people than allow a highly enlightened people to destroy his people through iniquity.
Alma recalls that the people received great favor and knowledge from the Lord.
Alma recounts spiritual visitations, conversation with angels, divine speech, prophecy, revelation, and spiritual gifts among their people.
Alma recalls deliverance from Jerusalem, famine, sickness, disease, bondage, and destruction in battle, and says they prospered and became rich.
Alma says transgression against their light and knowledge would make things more tolerable for the Lamanites than for them.
Alma says the Lord’s promises are extended to the Lamanites but warns that rebellious people will be destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues his address to the people.
